title: Error by AI scribe during medical appointment leaves patient devastated

reports.title: Error by AI scribe during medical appointment leaves patient devastated

summary:
Rebecca Green agreed to let an AI scribe transcribe her first urologist appointment, but the tool invented a claim that she micro-dosed psychedelic mushrooms. She only noticed the false statement after kidney stone surgery in March, when a post-operative letter to her GP said mushroom use might explain earlier kidney bleeding. Ms Green, who was on workers' compensation, feared the error could harm her case. The urologist later apologised, corrected the record, and said she would review how AI was used in her practice.

A Digital Rights Watch report found similar AI scribe mistakes, including recording the wrong breast in a cancer diagnosis and a false epilepsy claim. The Royal Australian College of GPs estimates 40 per cent of GPs regularly use AI scribes, though none are approved by the Therapeutic Goods Administration. The TGA has been reviewing these tools and will release findings in coming weeks, with breaches to be acted upon. Patient advocates want approved lists and stronger safeguards.
